Oct 25, 2026
95
DualShockers
Phantom Blade Zero is hands down the best action RPG this year, and quite honestly, one of the best action games I have played in a very long time. It has exceptional build variety, featuring an immense number of weapons and skills, all feeling distinct from each other and catering to different playstyles. It features a world filled with secrets, such as hidden bosses, storylines, and even completely optional regions, making exploration just as fantastic as its combat and progression systems. Despite its slight hiccups in performance, there's very little I'd change in S-Game's Phantom Blade Zero and I wouldn't be surprised if it ends up as a nominee for the grand prize at the Game Awards.

IGN Portugal
Phantom Blade Zero is a fantastic action game, underpinned by a combat system that borders on perfection. Whilst the narrative requires some patience at the outset and the design of the basic enemies fails to impress, the cast of epic bosses provides the perfect foil for the protagonists and their vast and impressive arsenal, which is brilliantly animated. Far from being just another run-of-the-mill game, it’s a fluid, visceral and incredibly rewarding dance. Long live Kungfupunk!

Console Creatures
The more I played Phantom Blade Zero, the more I fell in love with it. S-GAME has crafted an action RPG that delivers exactly what I've been craving: fast, fluid combat with an incredible arsenal of weapons, spectacular boss encounters and enough depth to keep me experimenting throughout the adventure. I wish the early story beats set the stage better and that some traversal mechanics and technical issues didn't interrupt the experience. But when I think back on my time with Phantom Blade Zero, what stands out are the incredible fights, the strange characters I encountered, and how often I wanted to keep playing.
PC FULL REVIEW
Oct 26, 2026
80
Gamekult
Playing Phantom Blade Zero means, first and foremost, accepting failure—especially when you find yourself embedded in the stone floor of an ancient temple, courtesy of a formidable opponent. And yet, while the game provides every reason to hurl your DualSense controller out the window, it also stands as an uncompromising display of artistic mastery: from its sumptuous visuals and eclectic soundtrack to its inventive arsenal and the sheer abundance of areas to explore. It offers moments of pure, wuxia-inspired grace—though these are framed by a narrative style that could best be described as rather disjointed. In short, it is a grand action game that transcends the sum of its parts, with the potential to become a true cult classic. Just keep an eye on its technical performance at launch.

Kahorn
Une aventure visuellement inégale, capable d'offrir des panoramas à couper le souffle, sublimés par de magnifiques musiques, mais aussi des environnements lointains manquant de vie et bien trop ternes, accompagnés de musiques plus que douteuses pour ce genre de jeu. Les combats, exigeants à maîtriser, sont particulièrement plaisants et satisfaisants, malgré quelques problèmes d'équilibrage qui rendent certains affrontements plutôt frustrants. Le jeu souffre également de freezes (surtout en cinématique) ainsi que de quelques crashs. Mais le plus gros problème reste l'histoire : une narration qui tend à être brouillonne, des allers-retours indigestes, une quantité excessive de notes à lire et un quest design aberrant, capable de vous imposer la mauvaise fin pour peu que vous ayez oublié de faire une activité secondaire des plus banales et inintéressantes ! Malgré un univers fascinant et de réelles qualités, difficile de ne pas ressortir frustré d'une aventure qui aurait pu être meilleure … Note objective sur 100 : 75. Note subjective sur 100 : 70. Temps de jeu : 48,7h. Succès : 51/66 (77%).

Kookaburra26
I also agree that a difficult game isn't necessarily a "Souls-like." But let’s be clear: The game was marketed as an Action-RPG adventure, and the marketing team explicitly stated that it would NOT have the same level of demands as games in the "Souls-like" genre. Naturally, players concluded that they wouldn't be facing "bullet-sponge" bosses (or rather, "HP-sponge" bosses) that unleash long combo chains, requiring precise parries and dodges with extremely punishing windows for counter-attacks.I acknowledge that there’s no respawn mechanic or loss of resources—fair enough. But look—if it takes you eight days (figuratively speaking) to take down a single boss, some people simply won't find that fun; had they known, they certainly wouldn't have bought the game. I understand that for those who enjoy this type of gameplay, the game might actually be too easy—but you also have to consider those for whom this is absolutely not their cup of tea. As I said, for me—and many others—this isn't at all the game I was expecting. There are several issues: the unacknowledged "Souls-lite" nature, the trailers that looked incredibly good... well, it *is* beautiful in places, but in others, it’s actually quite mediocre or even ugly. (I’m running it on a system with an RTX 5080, 64GB of RAM, and an i7 Ultra.) You might have a decent-looking panorama, but then you turn the camera and see rocks with low-resolution textures and jagged, poorly defined shapes. I’d love to get into the story (really! And i'm actually on the 3rd map), the lore, and the background, but honestly—it’s just poorly told! Crimson Desert was even better, and that wasn't even remotely the game's strong suit... Still, if some people are having fun, that’s great—honestly, I wish I could be like you and enjoy it, but... nope :'(
